t: #2605 — Form Smallest Number From Two Digit Arrays
o: Given two arrays of unique digits, build the smallest positive number containing at least one digit from each array. If the arrays share a digit (example 2: 3 appears in both), that single digit is optimal. Otherwise we need a two-digit number, and the smallest is the smaller of the two minimum digits as the tens digit and the other minimum as the units digit (example 1: 1 and 5 → 15).
k: A common digit always beats any two-digit answer.
Otherwise the answer uses the minimum of each array, arranged with the smaller digit in the tens place.

a.i: Compute the intersection of the two digit sets; if non-empty return its minimum. Otherwise let a = min(nums1), b = min(nums2) and return 10·min(a,b) + max(a,b).
s: Build sets from both arrays and intersect them.
If the intersection is non-empty, return its smallest element.
a.t: O(n1 + n2) — linear scans over both arrays.

w: Very easy; the only reasoning needed is why a shared digit dominates (it is a 1-digit number, smaller than anything with two digits) and why the smaller minimum belongs in the tens place. No real pitfalls beyond remembering digits are 1–9, never 0.
